Subject: NovaTech discovery — integration followups

Hi Sam — thanks again for the demo and context today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Priority outcomes you called out
  - Real-time chat assistant embedded in the product console that can call back-end services (customer profile, billing status) via tool-calls
  - A reranker that uses embeddings over product docs to surface high-precision results for support queries
  - Tight latency targets: ideally p95 < 500ms for conversational responses in the US region

2) Clarifying technical asks we promised to follow up on
  - SDK setup & auth options (public API keys vs mTLS / private deployment)
  - Routing policies: fallback to smaller/cheaper model under load; region-aware routing
  - Structured output/tool-calling: function signatures, JSON output enforcement
  - Embeddings & reranker: batch size, encoding, top-k strategy, refresh cadence for doc vectors
  - Request/response schema specifics: chat vs completions semantics, how tokenization affects max_tokens, recommended stop sequences, streaming behavior and partial outputs

Attachments: call recording + our initial POC mapping (novatech-poc-mapping.xlsx). I also added a short examples file (redwood-reqresp-examples.txt) with sample payload shapes we discussed.

Questions for you to confirm before we scope the POC: 
  a) Do you need the assistant to make authenticated calls to your internal APIs (yes/no)? If yes, will you provide a proxy endpoint or prefer the model to return a structured call spec that your client executes?
  b) Which UX is higher priority: instantaneous streaming tokens (chat-like) or fully validated JSON responses from the model for downstream processing?
  c) Any hard limits on token budget per request (we should size batch/quantization recommendations accordingly)?

Proposed next step: Ben (cc'd) can propose a concrete request/response schema and a short POC plan. Happy to set a 30-min kickoff next week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — great summary. A few clarifications that will help scope the POC: 

- Auth model: yes, the assistant must be able to trigger authenticated calls to our internal services. For security we prefer that the model returns a structured call description (function call) and our UI will execute the request through an auth proxy. We are not comfortable handing raw credentials to a third party process.

- Structured output: we need strict JSON for tool calls and for certain agent actions (create-ticket, lookup-account). Example expectation: {"action": "lookup_account", "params": {"account_id": "12345"}} — if the response is malformed we will reject it client-side.

- Chat vs completions: prefer chat with streaming for the UX of the console, but for backend batch reranking we expect completions-style calls. If streaming makes enforcing JSON harder, we can accept a two-step flow (stream for user UX, then a final validation pass).

- Token limits: for the first POC we can allow ~6k token budget per conversation (including history + response). We want to experiment with truncation strategies rather than strict hard caps initially.

- Embeddings/reranker: we'll maintain a vector store updated nightly (~100k docs), reranker should accept top-50 candidates and rerank top-5 with semantic scoring + recency signal. Latency target for rerank path: p95 < 350ms.

Procurement: looping in procurement@novatech.com for contracting questions.

Happy to go ahead with POC — if you can propose a short ask list and a one-week timeline for an internal spike, we'll confirm.

—Sam
Head of Product, NovaTech

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Apr 2028 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovaTech discovery — integration followups

Thanks — blocked time to sketch this out. Below are recommended defaults and example payloads. High-level notes first: 

Auth & deployment
- For POC: use hosted Redwood API with token-based auth from the client, but route tool-execution through NovaTech's auth proxy. Model never stores customer credentials (we only exchange function signatures / call specs). If NovaTech wants stronger isolation later, we can move to Dedicated or Private with mTLS + customer-managed KMS.

Routing & model variants
- Default routing: region-aware -> lowest-cost compatible model that meets latency SLO. Provide a canary path to an LLM variant with higher quality. Under overload, fallback to a quantized / smaller model for non-critical queries.

Streaming vs final validation
- Streaming UX: use token-streaming (SSE). For JSON/tool calling we recommend a hybrid: stream user-facing content, simultaneously produce a 'final_frame' that contains the canonical JSON payload (final_frame is emitted as a single event once generation ends). Client UI displays tokens as they stream but performs a validation pass on final_frame before executing any tool calls.
- Stop sequences: prefer explicit stop tokens for completion-style calls. For chat streaming, implement an end-of-turn marker (e.g., <|end_of_turn|>) that triggers assembly of final_frame.

Tokenization and max_tokens
- Tokens include both prompt/history and response. For safety, reserve at least 20% of max_tokens for the model's response when you need structured JSON. If total budget = 6000 tokens, cap input history at 4800 and set max_tokens=1200 for response. Use byte-pair tokenization norms — we will surface counts via the SDK so you can measure live.
- Truncation policy: prefer recency-first drop (drop oldest messages) for chat history. For search/rerank context, include only the top-k semantically similar docs and metadata (title, excerpt) to bound token counts.

Embeddings & reranker
- Recommend nightly index + incremental updates. For rerank: do a lightweight ANN search to fetch top-50 candidates, then run a supervised rerank pass (completions or dedicated reranker model) that scores each doc with context and returns top-5. Batch embeddings calls (batch size 64–256 depending on GPU memory) to lower cost and latency.

Example payloads (copy-paste friendly)
1) Chat streaming with final JSON frame (client executes final action):
Request (chat endpoint):
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-v1",
  "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant that returns a final JSON action frame."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Lookup account 12345 and state billing status."} ],
  "stream": true,
  "max_tokens": 800,
  "stop": ["<|end_of_turn|>"]
}

Server-side stream events (SSE):
- event: token
  data: "We found the account ..." (multiple token events)
- event: final_frame
  data: {"action": "lookup_account", "params": {"account_id": "12345"}}

Client behavior: show tokens as they stream; on final_frame validate JSON schema before calling the auth proxy.

2) Reranker (completions-style request):
Request (rerank endpoint):
{
  "model": "redwood-rerank-v1",
  "input": {"query": "how to reset password", "candidates": ["doc:987", "doc:444", "doc:123"], "metadata": {"top_k": 50} },
  "max_tokens": 256
}

Response: list of scored candidates with top-5 ids and scores. Keep the reranker as a synchronous, non-streaming path to keep p95 predictable.

Edge cases / validation
- If final_frame fails validation, client should fallback to human-in-the-loop review. Do not execute ambiguous actions.
- For streaming partial JSON fragments, do not attempt to execute until final_frame is received and validated.

Proposed POC scope & timeline
- Week 0 (engineering spike, 3 dev-days): implement chat endpoint + client streaming UX + final_frame validator.
- Week 1 (integration): wire the auth proxy, implement rerank path, load sample index (10k docs), run perf tests.
- Deliverable: interactive demo where agent returns a validated action for a lookup and a reranked list for search.

I'll prepare the sample request/response files (attached) and a short checklist for the kickoff.

—Ben
